problem_statement: In Rocket Chip's hypervisor two-stage address translation, the page-table walker (PTW) should validate the initial stage-2 guest physical address taken from the guest `vsatp` page-table base against the address-width rules implied by `hgatp.mode`. In the verified case, when that root guest physical address has non-zero upper bits above the range allowed by the active Sv39x4/Sv48x4/Sv57x4 mode, the PTW continues the walk instead of raising a guest-page fault. The affected logic is PTW validation of the stage-2 root address at the start of a virtualized translation request, and the expected behavior is to stop immediately with a guest-page fault whenever that root GPA is out of range.

title: Hypervisor: drive mtinst/htinst
body:
**Related issue**:

Doing this feature as required by the architecture:
> For guest-page faults, the trap instruction register is written with a special pseudoinstruction value if:
> (a) the fault is caused by an implicit memory access for VS-stage address translation, and
> (b) a nonzero value (the faulting guest physical address) is written to `mtval2` or `htval`.
> If both conditions are met, the value written to `mtinst` or `htinst` must be taken from the table below; zero is not allowed.

Paying off this tech debt from https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/pull/2841
> The `mtinst` and `htinst` CSRs are hardwired to 0, placing additional onus on hypervisor software to use the HLVX instruction.

**Type of change**: bug report | feature request

**Impact**: functional addition

**Development Phase**: implementation

**Release Notes**
Guest-page faults caused by an implicit memory access for VS-stage address translation write the architecturally-defined pseudo-instruction to `mtinst` or `htinst` because a nonzero value (the faulting guest physical address) is written to `mtval2` or `htval`.

resolved_issues.title: Add hypervisor extension
resolved_issues.body:
This PR implements v0.6.2 of the RISC-V Hypervisor Extension.

The implementation was inspired by José Martins' and colleagues' work
described in [1].  Much of the microarchitecture and essentially all of
the code is new, but their implementation served as our baseline.
We thank them for trailblazing hypervisor support in rocket-chip.

Note that this PR only includes the mechanisms to virtualize the hart
itself.  Virtualized interrupt controllers, IOMMUs, etc. are future work.
Lots of future work.

Note also that some features are (legally) not implemented.  Currently,
misa.H is not writable, something we may or may not choose to fix.
The mtinst and htinst CSRs are hardwired to 0, placing
additional onus on hypervisor software to use the HLVX instruction.

[1] "A First Look at RISC-V Virtualization from an Embedded Systems Perspective", https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14951

    nop
    nop
    nop
    nop
    nop

    nop
    nop
    nop
    nop
    nop
    nop

problem_statement: Observed behavior: in a Rocket core built with the hypervisor extension, the machine-level hypervisor trap-instruction CSR `mtinst` behaves as if it is hardwired to zero. If software writes a legal WARL value to `mtinst` and then reads it back, the read still returns zero. Expected behavior: `mtinst` must behave like an implemented hypervisor trap-instruction CSR, so a legal WARL write should be readable as a supported nonzero value instead of always reading as zero. Affected function: hypervisor trap-state and CSR handling for the `mtinst` trap-instruction register. Trigger condition: any hypervisor-enabled configuration where software directly accesses `mtinst`.

title: PTW: traverse check GPA bits higher than HGATP mode only if leaf
body:
**Related issue**: This is a similar bug as https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/pull/3625: different bits for a valid-but-table entry in the same last-level FSM state.

**Type of change**: bug report

**Impact**: functional fix

**Development Phase**: implementation

**Release Notes**
 PTW: qualify `invalid_gpa` with `pte.leaf()` instead of just `pte.v`.

**Related issue**: follow-on to https://github.com/chipsalliance/rocket-chip/pull/3591

**Type of change**: bug report

**Impact**: functional fix

**Development Phase**: implementation

**Release Notes**
PTW: qualify `invalid_gpa` with `pte.v` and all the other terms from `pf` (page fault) in `gf` (guest page fault).

diff --git a/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala b/src/main/scala/rocket/PTW.scala

@@ -695,7 +695,7 @@ class PTW(n: Int)(implicit edge: TLEdgeOut, p: Parameters) extends CoreModule()(
       when (do_both_stages && !stage2) { do_switch := true.B }

     }.otherwise {
-      val gf = (stage2 && !stage2_final && !pte.ur()) || (pte.v && pte.reserved_for_future === 0.U && invalid_gpa)
+      val gf = (stage2 && !stage2_final && !pte.ur()) || (pte.leaf() && pte.reserved_for_future === 0.U && invalid_gpa)
       val ae = pte.v && invalid_paddr
       val pf = pte.v && pte.reserved_for_future =/= 0.U
       val success = pte.v && !ae && !pf && !gf
@@ -723,7 +723,7 @@ class PTW(n: Int)(implicit edge: TLEdgeOut, p: Parameters) extends CoreModule()(
         }
 
         resp_ae_ptw := ae && count < (pgLevels-1).U && pte.table()
-        resp_ae_final := ae
+        resp_ae_final := ae && pte.leaf()

  val stage1Level0Table = tablePte(ppn = 0x234)
  val stage2MidLeaf0 = leafPte(ppn = BigInt(2) << 18, user = true)
  val stage1Level1Table = tablePte(ppn = 0x345)
  val stage2MidLeaf1 = leafPte(ppn = BigInt(3) << 18, user = true)
  val stage1Level2BadTable = tablePte(ppn = BigInt(1) << 30)
  val responseData = VecInit(Seq(
    stage2RootLeaf,
    stage1Level0Table,
    stage2MidLeaf0,
    stage1Level1Table,
    stage2MidLeaf1,
    stage1Level2BadTable
  ))

  val requestPending = RegInit(true.B)
  when (ptw.io.requestor(0).req.fire) {
    requestPending := false.B
  }

  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.valid := requestPending
  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.bits.valid := requestPending
  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.bits.bits.addr := 0.U
  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.bits.bits.need_gpa := false.B
  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.bits.bits.vstage1 := true.B
  ptw.io.requestor(0).req.bits.bits.stage2 := true.B

  val ptbr = 0.U.asTypeOf(new PTBR)
  ptbr.mode := 0.U
  ptbr.asid := 0.U
  ptbr.ppn := 0.U

  val vsatp = 0.U.asTypeOf(new PTBR)
  vsatp.mode := vsatp.pgLevelsToMode(3).U
  vsatp.asid := 0.U
  vsatp.ppn := 0x80.U

  val hgatp = 0.U.asTypeOf(new PTBR)
  hgatp.mode := hgatp.pgLevelsToMode(3).U
  hgatp.asid := 0.U
  hgatp.ppn := 0.U

  ptw.io.dpath.ptbr := ptbr
  ptw.io.dpath.vsatp := vsatp
  ptw.io.dpath.hgatp := hgatp
  ptw.io.dpath.sfence.valid := false.B
  ptw.io.dpath.sfence.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new SFenceReq)
  ptw.io.dpath.status := 0.U.asTypeOf(new MStatus)
  ptw.io.dpath.hstatus := 0.U.asTypeOf(new HStatus)
  ptw.io.dpath.gstatus := 0.U.asTypeOf(new MStatus)
  ptw.io.dpath.pmp := 0.U.asTypeOf(ptw.io.dpath.pmp)
  ptw.io.dpath.customCSRs := DontCare

  val reqCount = RegInit(0.U(3.W))
  val respDelay1Valid = RegInit(false.B)
  val respDelay2Valid = RegInit(false.B)
  val respDelay1Data = Reg(UInt(64.W))
  val respDelay2Data = Reg(UInt(64.W))

  when (ptw.io.mem.req.fire) {
    assert(reqCount < responseData.length.U, "PTW issued more memory requests than expected")
    respDelay1Valid := true.B
    respDelay1Data := responseData(reqCount)
    reqCount := reqCount + 1.U
  }.otherwise {
    respDelay1Valid := false.B
  }
  respDelay2Valid := respDelay1Valid
  respDelay2Data := respDelay1Data

  ptw.io.mem.req.ready := true.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_nack := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_nack_cause_raw := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_uncached := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_paddr := 0.U
  ptw.io.mem.resp.valid := respDelay2Valid
  ptw.io.mem.resp.bits := 0.U.asTypeOf(new HellaCacheResp)
  ptw.io.mem.resp.bits.data := respDelay2Data
  ptw.io.mem.replay_next := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.s2_xcpt := 0.U.asTypeOf(new HellaCacheExceptions)
  ptw.io.mem.s2_gpa := 0.U
  ptw.io.mem.s2_gpa_is_pte := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.ordered := true.B
  ptw.io.mem.store_pending := false.B
  ptw.io.mem.perf := 0.U.asTypeOf(new HellaCachePerfEvents)
  ptw.io.mem.clock_enabled := true.B

  val done = RegInit(false.B)
  when (ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.valid) {
    printf(p"PTW resp reqCount=${reqCount} gf=${ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.gf} ae_final=${ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.ae_final} gpa_is_pte=${ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.gpa_is_pte}\n")
    assert(reqCount === 6.U, "PTW responded after an unexpected number of memory requests")
    assert(ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.pte.table(), "Final PTW response should contain a valid table PTE")
    assert(ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.gpa_is_pte, "Final PTW response should still be marked as a GPA PTE")
    assert(!ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.gf, "PTW incorrectly raised guest fault on a valid table PTE")
    assert(!ptw.io.requestor(0).resp.bits.ae_final, "PTW incorrectly raised ae_final on a valid table PTE")
    done := true.B
  }

  io.done := done
}

object PTWGuestFaultRepro extends App {
  implicit val p: Parameters = new BaseSubsystemConfig
  simulate(LazyModule(new PTWGuestFaultDUT).module) { dut =>
    dut.reset.poke(true.B)
    dut.clock.step(2)
    dut.reset.poke(false.B)
    dut.clock.stepUntil(dut.io.done, 1, 80)
    dut.io.done.expect(true.B, "timed out waiting for PTW response")
  }
}
EOF
}

run_reproducer() {
  export PATH="$FIRTOOL_DIR/bin:$PATH"
  export VERILATOR_ROOT="$VERILATOR_COMPAT_ROOT"
  "$MILL_BIN" -i ptwRepro.runMain ptwrepro.PTWGuestFaultRepro
}

ensure_mill
ensure_firtool
ensure_verilator_root
ensure_build_module
write_repro_source

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
if run_reproducer; then
  echo "TEST: ptw_guest_fault_table_entry ... PASS"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  exit 0
else
  echo "TEST: ptw_guest_fault_table_entry ... FAIL"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
  exit 1
fi
problem_statement: Observed behavior: In Rocket's page-table walker (PTW), a hypervisor two-stage translation can incorrectly treat a valid non-leaf PTE (a page-table entry that points to the next page table) as a faulting final result when that entry's guest physical address contains bits above the range allowed by the active `hgatp` mode. In this case the PTW may return guest-page-fault and final access-error indications instead of returning the PTE as a valid table entry. Expected behavior: A valid non-leaf PTE in this situation must be returned as a table/page-pointer PTE, with no guest-page-fault and no final access error. The high-bit check against `hgatp` mode should affect leaf mappings, not table entries. Affected function: Rocket PTW handling of guest-physical-address validity during hypervisor VS-stage plus G-stage address translation. Trigger condition: A VS-stage plus G-stage walk reaches a valid table PTE in the final traversal step, and that PTE encodes guest-physical-address bits above the width permitted by the current `hgatp` mode.
